ce:2017:q1.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 1
ce:2017:q1.question: The matrix P is the inverse of a matrix Q. If $I$ denotes the identity matrix, which one of the following options is correct?

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given that P is inverse of Q.

$$\begin{aligned}   P&=Q^{-1}  & P&=Q^{-1} \\    PQ&=Q^{-1}Q &  QP&=QQ^{-1} \\    PQ&=I &  QP&=I \\ \therefore    PQ&=QP=I \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra

$f\left ( x \right )=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}$; $x=0$

ce:2017:q3.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 3
ce:2017:q3.question: Let x be a continuous variable defined over the interval ($-\infty ,\infty$), and $f(x)=e^{-x-e^{-x}}$. The integral $g(x)=\int f(x)dx$ is equal to

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right )&=e^{-x-e^{-x}}= e^{-x}.e^{-e^{-x}} \\  y\left ( x \right )&=\int f\left ( x \right )dx=\int e^{-x}.e^{-e^{-x}}dx\\ \text{Let }  e^{-x}&=t \\  -e^{-x}dx&=dt \\ \int f\left ( x \right )dx&=\int e^{-t}.\left ( -dt \right ) \\    &=\frac{e^{-t}}{-1}.\left ( -d \right ) \\    &=e^{-t} \\    &=e^{-\left ( e^{-x} \right )} \\ &=e^{-e^{-x}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2017:q5.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 5
ce:2017:q5.question: A simply supported beam is subjected to uniformly distributed load. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Maximum or minimum shear force occurs where the curvature is zero.
Maximum or minimum bending moment occurs where the shear force is zero.
Maximum or minimum bending moment occurs where the curvature is zero.
Maximum bending moment and maximum shear force occur at the same section.

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Shear Force & Bending Moment Differential Relationships
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Governing Principles & Differential Relations:**
  - In linear elastic beam theory, the relationship between load intensity $w(x)$, shear force $V(x)$, and bending moment $M(x)$ along the beam span is given by:
    $$\frac{dV}{dx} = -w(x)$$
    $$\frac{dM}{dx} = V(x)$$

- **Condition for Local Extrema of Bending Moment:**
  - By basic calculus, a continuous differentiable function $M(x)$ attains a local maximum or local minimum at points where its first derivative with respect to span location $x$ is equal to zero:
    $$\frac{dM}{dx} = 0 \implies V(x) = 0$$
  - Consequently, sections where the shear force is zero (or changes sign) are precisely the locations where the bending moment reaches its maximum or minimum values.

- **Application to a Simply Supported Beam with Uniformly Distributed Load (UDL):**
  - Consider a beam of span $L$ carrying a UDL of intensity $w$:
    $$R_A = R_B = \frac{wL}{2}$$
    $$V(x) = \frac{wL}{2} - wx$$
    $$M(x) = \frac{wLx}{2} - \frac{wx^2}{2}$$
  - The shear force is zero at $x = L/2$:
    $$V(L/2) = \frac{wL}{2} - w\left(\frac{L}{2}\right) = 0$$
  - At this exact section ($x = L/2$), the bending moment attains its absolute maximum:
    $$M_{\max} = \frac{wL^2}{8}$$

- **Distractor Analysis:**
  - **Option A is incorrect:** Curvature is $\kappa = \frac{1}{R} = \frac{M(x)}{EI}$. At the supports ($x = 0, L$), $M = 0 \implies \kappa = 0$, but the shear force is maximum ($|V| = wL/2$). Maximum shear force has no general correlation with zero curvature.
  - **Option C is incorrect:** Bending moment is zero (not maximum or minimum) where curvature is zero.
  - **Option D is incorrect:** For a simply supported beam with UDL, maximum shear force occurs at the end supports ($x = 0, L$), whereas maximum bending moment occurs at mid-span ($x = L/2$). They do not occur at the same section.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (Maximum or minimum bending moment occurs where the shear force is zero)**.

ce:2017:q11.question: A uniformly distributed line load of 500 kN/m is acting on the ground surface. Based on Boussinesq's theory, the ratio of vertical stress at a depth 2 m to that at 4 m, right below the line of loading, is

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Stress Distribution in the Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
$q^{\prime}=500 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}$

$x=0$ (Just below the line load)

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{z} &=\frac{2 q^{\prime}}{\pi z}\left(\frac{1}{1+\frac{x^{2}}{z^{2}}}\right)^{2}=\frac{2 q^{\prime}}{\pi z} \\ \text { Ratio } &=\frac{\left(\sigma_{z}\right)_{a t, 2 m}}{\left(\sigma_{z}\right)_{a t, 4 m}}=\frac{\frac{2 q^{\prime}}{\pi \times 2}}{\frac{2 q^{\prime}}{\pi \times 4}}=\frac{4}{2}=2 \end{aligned}$$

ce:2017:q17.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 17
ce:2017:q17.question: A runway is being constructed in a new airport as per the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) recommendations. The elevation and the airport reference temperature of this airport are 535 m above the mean sea level and 22.65$^{\circ}$C, respectively. Consider the effective gradient of runway as 1%. The length of runway required for a design-aircraft under the standard conditions is 2000 m. Within the framework of applying sequential corrections as per the ICAO recommendations, the length of runway corrected for the temperature is

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Railway and Airport Engineering
detailed_solution.markdown:
Elevation =535 m

Airport Reference Temperature $=22.65^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

Effective Gradient = 1%

Runway length =2000 m under standard conditions.

Runway length correction for $T^{\circ} \mathrm{C} .$

$\Rightarrow$Correction for elevation

$=\frac{7}{100} \times 2000 \times \frac{535}{300}=249.67 \mathrm{m}$

Corrected runway length $=2249.67 \mathrm{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ Corrected standard $T^{\circ}$ at 535 m elevation

$=15^{\circ} \mathrm{C}-(0.0065 \times 535)=11.52^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

Correction for $T^{\circ}$

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{100} \times 2249.67 \times \frac{\Delta T^{\circ} \mathrm{C}}{1^{\circ} \mathrm{C}} \\ \Delta T^{\circ} \mathrm{C} &=22.65-11.52=11.13^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=\frac{1}{100} \times 2249.67 \times \frac{11.13^{\circ} \mathrm{C}}{1^{\circ} \mathrm{C}} \\ &=250.39 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Corrected Runway length

$$\begin{array}{l} =2249.67+250.39 \\ =2500.06 \mathrm{m} \simeq 2500 \mathrm{m} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2017:q25.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 25
ce:2017:q25.question: Vehicles arriving at an intersection from one of the approach road follow the Poisson distribution. The mean rate of arrival is 900 vehicles per hour. ce:2017:q27.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ce:2017:q27.question: The solution of the equation $\frac{\mathrm{d} Q}{\mathrm{d} t}+Q=1$ with $Q=0$ at $t=0$ is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\mathrm{d} Q}{\mathrm{d} t}+Q=1$

Comparing with standard form, $I.F.=e^{\int 1dt}=e^{t}$

Solution is,

$$\begin{aligned}   Q.e^{t}&=\int 1.e^{t}dt=e^{t}+C \\    Q&=1+Ce^{-t} \;\;...(i) \\ \text{When }t&=0, Q=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;   0&=1+C \\ \Rightarrow \;\;   C&=-1 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, $Q\left ( t \right ) =1-e^{-t}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2017:q28.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 28
ce:2017:q28.question: Consider the matix $$\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1\\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$. Which one of the following statements is TRUE for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of this matrix?
options: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and only one independent eigenvector exists.
Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and two independent eigenvectors exist.
Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and no independent eigenvector exists.
Eigenvalues are 3 and -3, and two independent eigenvectors exist.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$A=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1\\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

Characteristic equation is $\left | A-\lambda I \right |=0$

$$\begin{aligned}     \begin{vmatrix} 5-\lambda & -1\\ 4 & 1-\lambda \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ 5-5\lambda -\lambda +\lambda ^{2}+4&=0 \\     \lambda ^{2}-6\lambda +9&=0 \\         \lambda &=3,\, 3 \end{aligned}$$

Algebraic multiplicity of eigen value 3 is 2. It has only one independent eigen vector exists.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

Based on the above observations, the correct statement is
options: bulk specific gravity of aggregate = 2.5 and water absorption = 2.5 %
bulk specific gravity of aggregate = 2.5 and water absorption = 2.4 %
apparent specific gravity of aggregate = 2.5 and water absorption = 2.5%
apparent specific gravity of aggregate = 2.5 and water absorption = 2.4 %

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Highway Materials
detailed_solution.markdown:
Bulk specific gravity $=\frac{A}{B-C}$

Apparent specific gravity $=\frac{A}{A-C}$

Where,

A= Mass of oven dry aggregate in air

B= Mass of Saturated surface dry aggregate in air

C= Mass of Saturated surface dry aggregate under water

$\therefore$ Bulk specific gravity

$=\frac{1000}{1025-625}=\frac{1000}{400}=2.5$

Water absorption

$=\frac{1025-1000}{1000} \times 100=2.5 \%$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2017:q33.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 33
ce:2017:q33.question:
The queue length (in number of vehicles) versus time (in seconds) plot for an approach to a signalized intersection with the cycle length of 96 seconds is shown in the figure.

At time t = 0, the light has just turned red. The effective green time is 36 seconds, during which vehicles discharge at the saturation flow rate, s (in vph). Vehicles arrive at a uniform rate, v (in vph), throughout the cycle. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: v = 600 vph, and for this cycle, the average stopped delay per vehicle = 30 seconds
s = 1800 vph, and for this cycle, the average stopped delay per vehicle = 28.125 seconds
v = 600 vph, and for this cycle, the average stopped delay per vehicle = 45 seconds
s = 1200 vph, and for this cycle, the average stopped delay per vehicle = 28.125 seconds

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Traffic Engineering
detailed_solution.markdown:
Vehicle arrived upto 60 sec (Red time) = 10

Arrival rate $= 1060 \times 3600=600 \; vph$

$v=600\; vph$

Departure at vehicle starts at 60 second and ends 90 seconds.

So, between 60 second to 90 second total vehicle departed

= Vehicle arrived upto 60 second + Vehicle arriving between 60 sec to 90 sec

$= 10 + 6003600 \times 30$

$= 10 + 5= 15$

So, departure rate = Saturation flow

$= s = 1530 \times 3600$

$s=1800\; vph$

Average delay time is given by

$t_d=\frac{\frac{C}{2}\left ( 1-\frac{g}{c} \right )^2}{1-\frac{v}{s}}$

C = 96 second

g = 96 -60 = 36 seconds

v = 600 Vph

s = 1800 Vph

$t_d=\frac{\frac{96}{2}\left ( 1-\frac{36}{96} \right )^2}{1-\frac{600}{1800}}$

$t_d=28.125 \; sec$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2017:q34.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 34
ce:2017:q34.question: The radius of a horizontal circular curve on a highway is 120 m. The design speed is 60 km/hour, and the design coefficient of lateral friction between the tyre and the road surface is 0.15. The estimated value of superelevation required (if full lateral friction is assumed to develop), and the value of coefficient of friction needed (if no superelevation is provided) will, respectively, be

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $R=120 \mathrm{m}, V=60 \mathrm{kmph}\text{ and }f=0.15$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad e+f&=\frac{v^{2}}{127 R} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e+0.15&=\frac{60^{2}}{127 \times 120} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e&=\frac{1}{11.6} \\ \text{Also, if }e&=0\\ \Rightarrow \quad f&=\frac{V^{2}}{127 R}=\frac{60^{2}}{127 \times 120} \simeq 0.24 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2017:q36.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 36
ce:2017:q36.question: The laboratory test on a soil sample yields the following results: natural moisture content = 18%, liquid limit = 60%, plastic limit = 25%, percentage of clay sized fraction = 25%. detailed_solution.markdown:

ce:2017:q37.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 37
ce:2017:q37.question: Consider the equation $\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}=3t^{2}+1$ with u=0 at t=0. This is numerically solved by using the forward Euler method with a step size $\Delta t= 2$. The absolute error in the solution at the end of the first time step is_________

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Numerical Methods
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}   \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\ f\left ( u,\: t \right )&=3t^{2}+1 \\ u_{0}&=0 \\ t_{0}&=0 \\ \Delta t&=2\\ &\text{By Euler's method} \\     u_{1}&=u_{0}+hf\left ( u_{0}t_{0} \right )  & t_{1}&=t_{0}+h \\     &=u_{0}+h\left ( 3t^{2}_{0}+1 \right )   &  &=0+2 \\     &=0+2\left ( 3\left ( 0 \right )^{2}+1 \right )   &  &=2 \\     &=2 \end{aligned}$$

After first iteration u=0 when t=2,

$$\begin{aligned}    \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\     du&=\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\    \int du&=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\     u&=\left.\begin{matrix} \left ( 3\frac{t^{3}}{3}+t \right ) \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{2} \\     &=8+2=10 \end{aligned}$$

Absolute error = Exact value - approx value

$=10-2 =8$

Therefore, the correct answer is **8** (acceptable range: [7.95, 8.05]).

ce:2017:q38.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 38
ce:2017:q38.question: A pre-tensioned rectangular concrete beam 150 mm wide and 300 mm depth is prestressed with three straight tendons, each having a cross-sectional area of 50 $mm^{2}$, to an initial stress of 1200 $N / mm^{2}$. The tendons are located at 100 mm from the soffit of the beam. If the modular ratio is 6, the loss of prestressing force (in kN, up to one decimal place) due to the elastic deformation of concrete only is ______

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Prestressed Concrete Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: Prestressing force, $$\begin{aligned} P&=3 \times 50 \times 1200=180000 \mathrm{N} \\ e&=\left(\frac{D}{2}-100\right)=\left(\frac{300}{2}-100\right)=50 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$ Stress in concrete at the location of steel $$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P \cdot e}{I} e\\ &=\frac{180000}{150 \times 300}+\frac{180000 \times 50^{2}}{\left(\frac{150 \times 300^{3}}{12}\right)} \\ &=4.0+1.33=5.333 \end{aligned}$$ Loss of stress $=m \times f_{c}=6 \times 5.3333=32 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}$ Loss of prestressing force $=\frac{3 \times 50 \times 32}{1000} \mathrm{kN}=4.8 \mathrm{kN}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **4.75** (acceptable range: [4.5, 5]).

ce:2017:q39.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 39
ce:2017:q39.question:
Consider the stepped bar made with a linear elastic material and subjected to an axial load of 1 kN, as shown in the figure.

Segments 1 and 2 have cross-sectional are of $100mm^{2}$ and $60mm^{2}$, Young's modulus of $2 \times 10^{5}$ MPa and $3 \times 10^{5}$ MPa, and length of 400mm and 900mm, respectively. The strain energy (in N-mm, up to one decimal place) in the bar due to the axial load is __________

primary.subtopicLabel: Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} A_{1}=100 \mathrm{mm}^{2}, & E I=2 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{MPa} \\ A_{2}=60 \mathrm{mm}^{2}, &E I=3 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{MPa} \\ \Delta_{A C}=&\Delta_{A B}+\Delta_{B C} \\ =& \frac{1 \times 10^{3} \times 400}{100 \times 2 \times 10^{5}}+\frac{1 \times 10^{3} \times 900}{60 \times 3 \times 10^{5}} \\ =& 0.02+0.05=0.07 \mathrm{mm} \\ U=\frac{1}{2} \times P \times \Delta&=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 1000 \times 0.07=35 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **35** (acceptable range: [34.9, 35.1]).

ce:2017:q42.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ce:2017:q42.question: Consider two axially loaded columns, namely, 1 and 2, made of a linear elastic material with Young's modulus $2 \times 10^{5}$  MPa, square cross- section with side 10 mm, and length 1 m. For Column 1, one end is fixed and the other end is free. For Column 2, one end is fixed and the other end is pinned. Based on the Euler's theory, the ratio (up to one decimal place) of the buckling load of Column 2 to the buckling load of Column 1 is ________

primary.subtopicLabel: Theory of Columns and Shear Centre

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Theory of Columns and Shear Centre
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} P_{c r 1}&=\frac{\pi^{2} E \cdot I}{(2 l)^{2}}=\frac{\pi^{2} E I}{4 l^{2}} \\ P_{c r 2}&=\frac{\pi^{2} E \cdot I}{\left(\frac{l}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}}=\frac{2 \pi^{2} E I}{l^{2}}\\ \therefore \text{Required ratio }&=\frac{P_{C r 2}}{P_{c r 1}}=\frac{\frac{2 \pi^{2} E I}{l^{2}}}{\frac{\pi^{2} E I}{4 l^{2}}}=8 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **8.1** (acceptable range: [7.9, 8.3]).

ce:2017:q43.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 43
ce:2017:q43.question:
A column is subjected to a load through a bracket as shown in the figure.

The resultant force (in kN, up to one decimal place) in the bolt 1 is_____

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Structural Fasteners
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} F_{1}&=\frac{P}{n}=\frac{10}{4}=2.5kN \\ F_{2}&=\frac{Pe}{\sum r^{2}_{i}}\times r_{1} \\&=\frac{10\times 15}{4\times 5^{2}}\times 5=7.5 kN \\ F_{R}&=\sqrt{F^{2}_{1}+F_{2}^{2}+2F_{1}F_{2}\cos \theta } \\ &=\sqrt{2.5^{2}+7.5^{2}+2\times 2.5\times 7.5\times \cos 135^{\circ}} \\ &=6kN \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **6** (acceptable range: [5.9, 6.1]).

ce:2017:q44.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ce:2017:q44.question: A particle of mass 2 kg is travelling at a velocity of 1.5 m/s. A force $f(t)=3t^{2}$  (in N) is applied to it in the direction of motion for a duration of 2 seconds, where t denotes time in seconds. The velocity (in m/s, up to one decimal place) of the particle immediately after the removal of the force is _____

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}m=2 kg, \; V_{0}&=1.5\: m/sec \\  \int_{0}^{t}F\left ( t \right )dt &= m\left ( V-V_{0} \right ) \\  \int_{0}^{2}3t^{2}dt &= 2\left ( V-1.5 \right ) \\  \left [ t^{3} \right ]_{0}^{2} &= 2\left ( V-1.5 \right ) \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  \left ( 8-0 \right ) &= 2\left ( V-1.5 \right ) \\   V&=5.5\: m/s \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **5.5** (acceptable range: [5.4, 5.6]).

ce:2017:q46.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 46
ce:2017:q46.question: It is proposed to drive H-piles up to a depth of 7 m at a construction site. The average surfacearea of the H-pile is 3 $m^{2}$ per meter length. The soil at the site is homogeneous sand, havingan effective friction angle of 32$^{\circ}$. The ground water table (GWT) is at a depth of 2 m below the ground surface. The unit weights of the soil above and below the GWT are 16 $kN/m^{3}$ and 19 $kN/m^{3}$ respectively. Assume the earth pressure coefficient, K= 1.0, and the angle of wall friction $\delta =23^{\circ}$, The total axial frictional resistance (in kN, up to one decimal place) mobilized on the pile against the driving is _____

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Deep Foundation
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} Q_{s t} &=\frac{1}{2} k \gamma L_{1} \tan \delta A_{s_{1}}+\frac{1}{2} K\left[\gamma L_{1}+\gamma^{\prime} L_{2}\right] \tan \delta A_{s_{2}} \\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 16 \times 2 \tan 23^{\circ}(3 \times 2) \\ &+\frac{1}{2} \times 1[16 \times 2+77.95] \times \tan 23^{\circ}(5 \times 3) \\ &=390.8 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **388.5** (acceptable range: [385, 392]).

ce:2017:q47.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ce:2017:q47.question:
The infinite sand slope shown in the figure is on theverge of sliding failure. The ground water tablecoincides with the ground surface. Unit weight of water $\gamma _{w}=9.81\; kN/m^{3}$.

The value of the effective angle of internal friction (indegrees, up to one decimal place) of the sand is________

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Stability Analysis of Slopes
detailed_solution.markdown:
Infinite sand slope:

GWT coincides with the ground surface, therefore

$F.O.S. =\frac{\gamma^{\prime}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}} \times \frac{\tan \phi^{\prime}}{\tan \beta}$

As slope is on the verge of sliding failure hence,

$$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{F} \mathrm{O} . \mathrm{S}=\frac{\gamma^{\prime} \tan \phi^{\prime}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}} \tan \beta}=1\\ (21-9.81) \tan \phi^{\prime}=21 \tan 20^{\circ} \\ \phi=34.3^{\circ} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **34.25** (acceptable range: [34, 34.5]).

ce:2017:q48.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ce:2017:q48.question:
A sluice gate used to control the flow in a horizontal channel of unit width is shown in the figure.

It is observed that the depth of flow is 1.0 m upstream of the gate, while the depth is 0.2 m downstream of the gate. Assuming a smooth flow transition across the sluice gate, i.e., without any energy loss, and the acceleration due to gravity as 10 $m/s^{2}$ the discharge (in $m^{3}/ s$, up to two decimal places) passing under the sluice gate is_____

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
Applying Bernoulli's energy balance equation

$$\begin{aligned} y_{1}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g A_{1}^{2}}&=y_{2}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g A_{2}^{2}}\\ \text{Given }\quad y_{1}=1 \mathrm{m}, b&=1 \mathrm{m}, \quad y_{2}=0.2 \\ \Rightarrow 1+\frac{q^{2} \times 1^{2}}{2 g(1 \times 1)^{2}}&=0.2+\frac{q^{2} \times 1^{2}}{2 g \times(0.2 \times 1)^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.8 &=\frac{q^{2}}{2 g}\left(\frac{1}{(0.2)^{2}}-1\right) \\ 0.8 &=\frac{q^{2}}{20} \times 24 \\ q &=0.816 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.815** (acceptable range: [0.8, 0.83]).

ce:2017:q49.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 49
ce:2017:q49.question:
Water flows through a 90$^{\circ}$ bend in a horizontal plane as depicted in the figure.

A pressure of 140 kPa is measured at section 1-1. The inlet diameter marked at section 1-1 is $\frac{27}{\sqrt{\pi }}cm$, while the nozzle diameter marked at section 2-2 is $\frac{14}{\sqrt{\pi }}cm$. Assume the following:

(i) Acceleration due to gravity = 10 $m/s^{2}$
(ii) Weights of both the bent pipe segment as well as water are negligible.
(iii) Friction across the bend is negligible.

The magnitude of the force (in kN, up to two decimal places) that would be required to hold the pipe section is ______

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Dynamics and Flow Measurements
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} P_{1} A_{1} &=F_{x} \\ F_{x} &=\left(140 \times 10^{3}\right)\left[\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{0.27}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{2}\right] \\ &=2551.5 \mathrm{N}\\ F_{y} &=P_{2} A_{2} \\ &=\left(1.013 \times 10^{5}\right)\left[\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{0.14}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{2}\right] \\ &=49637 \mathrm{N} \\ \text { Resultant force } &=\sqrt{F_{x}^{2}+F_{y}^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{(2551.5)^{2}+(49637)^{2}} \\ &=259933 \mathrm{N} \\ &=2.60 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **3.125** (acceptable range: [2.5, 3.75]).

ce:2017:q50.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 50
ce:2017:q50.question: A consolidated undrained $\bar{CU}$ triaxial compression test is conducted on a normally consolidated clay at a confining pressure of 100 kPa. The deviator stress at failure is 80 kPa, and the pore-water pressure measured at failure is 50 kPa. The effective angle of internalfriction (in degrees, up to one decimal place) of the soil is _________

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shear Strength of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
CU test is conducted.

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{3}= 100 &\mathrm{kPa}, \sigma_{a}=80 \mathrm{kPa}, u=50 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \sigma_{1}&=\sigma_{3}+\sigma_{d} =100+80=180 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\sigma_{1}-u= 180-50=130 \mathrm{kPa}\\ \bar{\sigma}_{3}&=\sigma_{3}-u=100-50=50 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right)+2 C^{\prime} \tan \left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ \text{Assume }\quad C^{\prime}&=0 \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ 130&=50 \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ \phi^{\prime}&=26.4^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **26.25** (acceptable range: [25.5, 27]).

ce:2017:q51.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 51
ce:2017:q51.question: An effective rainfall of 2-hour duration produced a flood hydrograph peak of 200 $m^{3}/s$. The flood hydrograph has a base flow of 20 $m^{3}/s$. If the spatial average rainfall in the watershed for the duration of storm is 2 cm and the average loss rate is 0.4 cm/hour, the peak of 2-hour unit hydrograph (in $m^{3}/s-cm$, up to one decimal place) is _____

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Infiltration, Runoff and Hydrographs
detailed_solution.markdown:
Peak of 2 hr direct runoff hydrograph = Peak of 2 hr flood hydrograph-Base flow

=200-20

=180 $m^{3}/sec.$

The rainfall excess depth for a given duration of 2 hr effective storm/rainfall is given by,

Rainfall excess depth

$=2 cm-0.4 \frac{cm}{hr}\times 2 hr$

$=1.2 cm$

$\therefore$Peak of 2 hr UH

$=\frac{180}{1.2}=150 m^{3}/s-cm$

Therefore, the correct answer is **150** (acceptable range: [149, 151]).

ce:2017:q52.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 52
ce:2017:q52.question: The equivalent sound power level (in dB) of the four sources with the noise levels of 60 dB, 69 dB, 70 dB and 79 dB is_______

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} L_{eq} &=10\log_{10}\left [ \sum 10^{\frac{L_{i}}{10}} \right ] \\ &=10\log_{10}\left ( 10^{\frac{60}{10}}+10^{\frac{69}{10}}+10^{\frac{70}{10}}+10^{\frac{79}{10}} \right ) \\ &=79.9\: \text{dB} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **80** (acceptable range: [79, 81]).

ce:2017:q53.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 53
ce:2017:q53.question:
The spherical grit particles, having a radius of 0.01mm and specific gravity of 3.0, need to beseparated in a settling chamber. It is given that

$g=9.81 \; m/s^{2}$
the density of the liquid in the settling chamber $=1000 \; kg/m^{3}$
the kinematic viscosity of the liquid in the settling chamber = $10^{-6} \; m^{2}/s$

Assuming laminar conditions, the settling velocity (in mm/s, up to one decimal place) is_____

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} v_{s} &=\frac{(G-1) g d^{2}}{18 v}=\frac{(3-1) 9.81\left(0.02 \times 10^{-3}\right)^{2}}{18 \times 10^{-6}} \times 10^{3} \\ &=0.436 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.4** (acceptable range: [0.3, 0.5]).

ce:2017:q54.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 54
ce:2017:q54.question:
Two wastewater streams A and B, having an identical ultimate BOD are getting mixed to form the stream C. The temperature of the stream A is 20$^{\circ}$C and the temperature of the stream C is 10$^{\circ}$C. It is given that

The 5-day BOD of the stream A measured at 20$^{\circ}$C=50 mg/l
BOD rate constant (base 10) at 20$^{\circ}$C=0.115 per day
Temperature coefficient = 1.135

The 5-day BOD (in mg/l, up to one decimal place)of stream C, calculated at 10$^{\circ}$C, is ______

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{At A,}\; \; \; \left ( BOD_{5} \right )_{20^{\circ}C}&=L\left ( 1-10^{-k_{D}20^{\circ}C\times 5} \right ) \\ 50 &=L\left ( 1-10^{-0.115\times 5} \right ) \\ L&= 68.129\; mg/l\\ \text{Here,} \; \; k_{D_{10}}&=k_{D_{20}}\times \left [ 1.135 \right ]^{10-20} \\ &=0.115\times \left ( 1.135 \right )^{-10} \\ &=0.0324 \\ \text{For C,}\; \;\left ( BOD_{5} \right )_{10^{\circ}C} &=L\left [ 1-10^{-k_{D_{10\times 4}}} \right ] \\ &=68.13\left [ 1-10^{-0.0324\times 5} \right ] \\ &=21.21\; mg/l \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **21** (acceptable range: [20, 22]).

ce:2017:q55.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | Question: 55
ce:2017:q55.question: The wastewater having an organic concentration of 54 mg/l is flowing at a steady rate of 0.8 $m^{3}/day$ through a detention tank of dimensions $2m\times 4m\times 2m$. If the contents of the tankare well mixed and the decay constant is 0.1 per day, the outlet concentration (in mg/l, up to one decimal place) is ______

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
$Q=0.8 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{d}$

Detention time,

$$\begin{aligned} D_{t}&=\frac{V}{Q}=\frac{4 \times 2 \times 2 \mathrm{m}^{3}}{0.8 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{day}}=20 \mathrm{days} \\ L_{t}&=\frac{L_{0}}{1+k_{\mathrm{e}} t}=\frac{54}{1+0.1 \times 20}=18 \mathrm{mg} / l \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **18** (acceptable range: [17.9, 18.1]).

ce:2017:ga:q3.title: GATE CE 2017 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 3
ce:2017:ga:q3.question:
Consider the following sentences:
All benches are beds. No bed is a bulb. Some bulbs are lamps.
Which of the following can be inferred?
